top.line: Why a web of trust works now: commodity primitives, an engine the user never sees, links that count both ways.

in-short.line: Earlier failures, commodity primitives, a transparent engine, two-way links, provenance, hard to game.

why-now.line: Earlier key stores failed for want of workflows; the February briefs had the ideas; the pieces are now commodity.

primitives.line: A site per person, mature PKI, keys anywhere, git, QR codes, and an agent engine, even a small model.

direction.line: Anyone can link to anyone; only returned links count; a page holds only its owner's links.

provenance.line: Kinds plus date, place and event make links confirmable; agents nudge; checks mostly in code.

fractal.line: Each owner defines their schema; only nodes, edges and signatures stay constant.

security.line: Easy to game one node, hard to game them all at once.

identity.line: Open identity at scale, author-signed content, and every identity provider as evidence.

standard.line: Next: a small standard for keys, links, claims, confirmation and walking the graph.

limits.line: Kinds and provenance proposed; small models a bet; DNS later.

sources.line: My thinking, my February and March briefs, and pki.sgit.ai, on 21 November 2026.
